sources.citation: Mietzner, Angelika & Anne Storch (eds.). 2015. Nilo-Saharan – Models and Descriptions (NSLC-11 proceedings). Köln: Köppe — table of contents
sources.note: Checked only to see whether Kutsch Lojenga's 2013 NSLC paper was published there: it was not (23 chapters, none on Mvuba).

sources.citation: OLAC. 'OLAC resources in and about the Mvuba language' (language-archives.org/language/mxh; Wayback snapshot 2026-06-13, data as of 2025-11-04)
sources.note: No archived descriptive resource for mxh anywhere in OLAC (only Glottolog, Ethnologue and LINGUIST List stubs) — i.e. no SIL survey or phonology write-up is archived for Mvuba.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue, 19th ed., entry 'Mvuba' (Wayback snapshot 2016-03-04)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone (no typology line). 5,100 speakers in DRC (2000), Nord-Kivu, Beni territory, Oicha area; 'Dialects: None known. Reportedly similar to Lese [les].'

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Mvuba (mvub1239) and any-field bibliography search 'Mvuba' (4 records)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Confirms the complete Glottolog descriptive literature for Mvuba is Lomami Makala 2012 and Kutsch Lojenga 2013 (plus van Geluwe 1957, ethnographic); subclassification ref Vorbichler 1965 pp. 1-13.
No phonology content; cites only Ethnologue 18 and non-linguistic web pages.

sources.citation: Vorbichler, Anton. 1965. Die Phonologie und Morphologie des Balese (Ituri-Urwald, Kongo). Glückstadt: J. J. Augustin. (Afrikanistische Forschungen 2)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: library print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan): WID Offsite Storage 2235.185 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Full phonology of the closest relative, Lese (lese1243), to which Mvuba is 'reportedly similar'; would give the prosodic type (tone vs. accent) of the Nuclear Baleseic group and its pp. 1-13 discuss Mvuba's position — second-hand for Mvuba itself.

sources.citation: Van Geluwe, H. 1957. Mamvu-Mangutu et Balese-Mvuba. Ethnographic Survey of Africa, Central Africa: Belgian Congo, part 3. Tervuren: Musée Royal du Congo Belge. xi+195 pp. (Routledge reprint 2017)

sources.note: Ethnographic survey with a short language section on Balese-Mvuba; unlikely to state stress, but it is the only other work Glottolog indexes for Mvuba and may cite earlier missionary wordlists or notes on the language.
